techniques.name: Flat out to the brake marker
techniques.summary: Stay flat out in a straight line right up to your braking point; don't lift before it.
techniques.notes: Ed's brief, point 1, and his checklist row on lift-and-coast before the brake zone. Recorded (pitwall_patch_review): Ed's lift-before-braking scan fired on 23.2% of real F1 25 corner-laps, inflated by a scan bug that reports hundreds of metres, so pre_brake_coast_m is not trusted yet.
techniques.detail: Any distance off the throttle before the brake goes on is spent neither accelerating nor braking hard, so the throttle comes off and the brake goes on in one quick movement. When the race strategy asks for fuel saving, lift and coast replaces this on purpose.

techniques.name: Lift and coast to save fuel
techniques.summary: When the race asks for fuel saving, lift off the throttle a little before the braking zone, let the car roll to it, then brake as usual.
techniques.notes: The legitimate form of Ed's lift-before-braking row: when the strategy asks for fuel saving, the lift is intended, so a lift_before_braking fault should not be said to that driver.
techniques.detail: Fuel burns fastest at full throttle at top speed, so a short lift at the end of a straight saves the most fuel for the least time: the car's drag slows it while the engine idles, and the stop begins from a little less speed, which also cools the brakes and the engine. Here a lift before the brake is a strategy choice, not a fault.

techniques.name: Fast brake attack
techniques.summary: Get to peak brake pressure almost at once, rather than squeezing up to it.
techniques.notes: Ed's brief, point 2; his checklist row on a slow ramp-up. Recorded (pitwall_patch_review): on real F1 25 laps the time-to-peak delta against the reference spans p10 -0.16 s to p90 +0.23 s, so a few hundredths are noise.
techniques.detail: The car can slow hardest at the start of the stop, while the speed - and in a downforce car the aero grip - is highest, so the peak pressure belongs right at the beginning of the braking zone. A slow build wastes the first metres of the stop. Too sudden a stab can lock a wheel or bounce the car on its suspension: the right rate depends on the car and its tyres.

techniques.name: Progressive brake release
techniques.summary: Ease the brake pressure off smoothly as the car slows, rather than letting it go all at once.
techniques.notes: Ed's brief, point 3; his checklist rows on an abrupt or stepped release and on a double hump. Recorded (pitwall_patch_review): the release-time delta against the reference spans p10 -0.48 s to p90 +0.43 s on real F1 25 laps, so the release shape varies a lot from lap to lap.
techniques.detail: As the speed falls the tyres need less pressure to stay at their limit - in a downforce car because the aero grip falls with the speed too - so the pressure bleeds steadily down from its peak. In a low-downforce car it can stay near the peak for longer before the smooth release. A pedal let go in one step throws the load off the front tyres at once and can leave the car pushing wide at turn-in; lifting and pressing again mid-stop unsettles it the same way.

techniques.name: Rev-matched downshifts
techniques.summary: With a manual gearbox, blip the throttle on each downshift while braking, so the revs match and the rear stays settled.
techniques.notes: Ed's brief, point 4; his missed-blips count (root-cause patch). Recorded (pitwall_patch_review): 69% of real F1 25 downshifts have no driver throttle near them, because the game blips on paddle downshifts; the count means nothing there, hence the h_pattern condition (unknown gearbox = does not apply).
techniques.detail: On a downshift the engine has to spin faster to match the wheels in the lower gear. A blip of the throttle does that - heel and toe: the right foot on the brake and the throttle at once. Without it the engine briefly drags on the driven wheels, which can lock them or unsettle the rear in the braking zone. The downshifts are done while braking, before the car turns in, so no gear change lands while it is loaded in the corner. Only for an H-pattern gearbox with a clutch: paddle-shift cars blip by themselves, so their throttle trace never shows it.

techniques.name: Straight-line braking
techniques.summary: Do all the braking with the wheel straight, and be fully off the brake before you turn in.
techniques.notes: Ed's brief, point 5. Recorded (pitwall_style_review, 2026-10-15): the owner's fastest F1 25 laps trail-brake into 40 of 41 braking corners (median 33 m of braking with the wheel turned), and within a corner more trail braking went with a faster corner in 28 of 45 corners (median r -0.13): a weak effect, against this technique for that driver and car - which is why it applies only when one of its conditions holds.
techniques.detail: Braking and turning are kept apart, so each gets all of the tyres' grip and only one input changes at a time: the car stays calm and the brake point is easy to repeat. It is how drivers are usually taught first, and it suits a car without ABS and with little downforce, where braking hard while turning can lock the front tyres. The cost is grip left unused while the car changes from braking to turning; trail braking is the alternative that blends the two.

techniques.name: A consistent brake marker
techniques.summary: Brake at the same marker, the same way, every lap, so each change you try can be judged.
techniques.notes: Ed's checklist row on lap-to-lap scatter at one corner (and his suggestion to make it a signal of its own). Pitwall computes the spread after the session (CornerSummary.brake_point_std_m), not live.
techniques.detail: A repeatable brake point, turn-in and apex make each lap a baseline: when one thing changes, the lap time and the traces show whether it helped. Brake points that wander from lap to lap are one of the commonest signs of inconsistency, and they hide what is really costing time. A fixed visual reference for each braking zone - a board, a kerb, a shadow - is what makes it repeatable.

techniques.name: Left-foot braking
techniques.summary: Brake with the left foot while the right stays on the throttle; a short, deliberate overlap of the two pedals is part of the technique.
techniques.notes: Makes intentional pedal overlap legitimate (Ed's checklist row on unintentional overlap). Pitwall cannot yet tell which foot brakes, so it only knows the car allows it. Recorded (pitwall_patch_review): Ed's pedal-overlap detector fires on 66.8% of real F1 25 corner-laps because F1 25 reports about 0.10 throttle under braking - a game artefact, not the driver's feet.
techniques.detail: Possible in cars with no clutch pedal to work: paddle shifts or automatic gears. It saves moving one foot between the pedals, and a touch of brake with the throttle still on can settle the car or help it rotate, so brake and throttle overlapping is intended here, not a fault. The left foot's feel takes practice, and it is optional: many drivers stay quicker braking with the right foot.

techniques.name: Trail braking
techniques.summary: Keep some brake on as you start to turn, and ease it off as the steering goes in.
techniques.notes: The alternative to Ed's points 5, 6 and 8 (straight-line braking, off the brake with speed to spare, coasting to the apex) for trail-braking drivers and high-downforce cars. Recorded (pitwall_style_review, 2026-10-15): the owner's fastest F1 25 laps trail-brake into 40 of 41 braking corners (median 33 m of braking with |steering| >= 0.08), and within a corner across clean laps more trail braking went with a faster corner in 28 of 45 corners (median r -0.13): a weak effect, in favour of this technique for that driver and car.
techniques.detail: The brake pressure left on past turn-in keeps load on the front tyres so the car turns and rotates, and the release is blended with the steering - the pressure falling roughly in step as the wheel goes in, gone by the apex - so the tyres stay near their grip limit the whole way. It suits high-downforce cars and drivers who already brake this way; it asks for a fine feel for the release, and too much brake while turning makes the front tyres slide.

techniques.name: Off the brake with speed to spare
techniques.summary: Come off the brake with a little speed to spare and let the cornering load slow the car to the apex.
techniques.notes: Ed's brief, point 6. Not an instruction to release the brake at another point than the driver does: Pitwall never tells a driver to release earlier or carry more speed in (constraints.toml); this describes the straight-line technique.
techniques.detail: In the straight-line style the brake is fully released just before turn-in, deliberately while the car is still a little faster than the apex needs; as the wheel goes in, the tyres' cornering load scrubs off the rest. The opposite is reaching the apex already too slow, with nothing left for the corner to take off. A trail-braking driver does the same job with the brake still easing off during turn-in.

techniques.name: One smooth turn-in
techniques.summary: Turn in smoothly to the steering the corner needs in one movement, then hold it; no sawing at the wheel.
techniques.notes: Ed's brief, point 7; his checklist rows on sawing mid-corner and a snatched turn-in. Recorded (pitwall_patch_review): Ed's steering-reversal count fired on 22.6% of real F1 25 corner-laps, with 3 to 5 reversals per corner even on clean laps, so small corrections are normal and the threshold is not validated.
techniques.detail: One clean input lets the tyres build their cornering load progressively and the car settle on its line. A snatched turn-in can overload the front tyres or make the rear step out, and corrections back and forth mid-corner scrub speed and usually mean the car's balance or the line is not right. In a trail-braking corner the steering still goes in once, while the brake eases off.

techniques.name: Coast to the apex
techniques.summary: Between the brake and the throttle, stay off both pedals and let the cornering load scrub off the last of the speed to the apex.
techniques.notes: Ed's brief, point 8. Tier brief, not expert: published telemetry guides mostly read a long coast as braking that finished too soon (mysimrig_telemetry_beginners, hpa_braking_technique); NASA's release article only notes that the car keeps slowing with the brake off. Recorded (pitwall_style_review, 2026-10-15): on the owner's fastest F1 25 laps the car coasts 10 m or more at 15% of corners (median 0 m), and within a corner more coasting went with a slower corner in 22 of 35 corners (median r +0.12): weak, against this technique for that driver and car.
techniques.detail: With the brake fully off before turn-in, the car is still slowing as it turns: the tyres' cornering load takes off the remaining speed with no pedal to unsettle it, and the driver can feel the balance before picking up the throttle. It belongs with straight-line braking. Telemetry guides usually read a long gap off both pedals as time lost; for a trail-braking driver the brake easing off to the apex does this job instead.

techniques.name: Throttle once the car has rotated
techniques.summary: At the apex, once the car is pointing where you want it, squeeze the throttle on in one smooth, progressive application.
techniques.detail: At the apex the tyres are giving all their grip to cornering, with little or no pedal. Once the car has turned enough, the throttle comes in progressively, and the tyres take more drive as the steering unwinds. Picking it up before the car has rotated tends to make it push wide and keeps the steering on longer, which delays full throttle.

techniques.name: Commit to the throttle
techniques.summary: Once the throttle is on, keep it rising to full; no lift part-way through.
techniques.notes: Ed's brief, point 10, and his self-check (an on-off-on throttle means over-braking), which the causes keep as a review-only explanation tied to the driver's own faster laps, never an instruction. His checklist rows on a sawtooth throttle and his throttle_modulation detector. Recorded (pitwall_patch_review): the throttle-dip detector fired on 5.1% of real F1 25 corner-laps.
techniques.detail: Each lift after the pick-up delays full throttle and unsettles the car as the load moves forward again. A lift part-way through the exit usually points back to the entry: the car reached the apex slower than it could have, or was turned in too early and ran short of road - the driver's own faster laps at that corner show which. An on-off-on throttle trace is the signature.

techniques.name: Unwind as the throttle goes on
techniques.summary: Open the steering as you add throttle, so the wheel is straight by the time you are flat out.
techniques.notes: Ed's brief, point 11; his checklist rows on throttle before the steering unwinds (power understeer), the throttle acceptance KPI (lateral g at full throttle over the corner's peak) and the mid-corner unwind rate. Recorded (pitwall_patch_review): the low-throttle-acceptance detector fired on 6.0% of real F1 25 corner-laps, with its wording inverted.
techniques.detail: The tyres' grip is shared between cornering and drive: as the steering comes off, the grip it frees goes to acceleration. Full throttle with a lot of steering still on asks more than the tyres have - the car pushes wide or the rear steps out - while a wheel straightened long before full throttle leaves exit speed unused.

techniques.name: Use all the track on exit
techniques.summary: Let the car run out to the edge of the track on exit, and change up as normal.
techniques.notes: Ed's brief, point 12. No measured_by: track width needs the track edges, which no game sends; exit speed and full-throttle point show the effect, not the cause.
techniques.detail: Using the whole width opens the corner's radius, so the steering can come off and the throttle reach full sooner. A car that finishes the exit well inside the edge has turned tighter than it needed to. Pitwall does not know where the track edges are, so it cannot measure this directly yet.

signals.summary: Where braking ended on this lap minus the reference lap; below zero means braking ended sooner.

signals.summary: How long the brake took to come off from near its peak, this lap minus the reference lap; below zero is quicker.

signals.name: Minimum speed
signals.summary: The corner's slowest speed on this lap.
signals.notes: The incident rule compares it with the reference lap's: below INCIDENT_SPEED_FRAC of a reference of at least INCIDENT_MIN_REF_KPH is a crawl, not a technique difference.

signals.name: Full throttle point
signals.summary: Where full throttle came after the corner's slowest point on this lap.
signals.notes: BrakingEvent.throttle_full_m (analysis.braking.THROTTLE_FULL); the late_throttle rule reads its delta.

signals.name: Trail-braking distance
signals.summary: How far the car travels on the brake with the wheel turned, in one braking zone.
signals.notes: Braking with |steering| above analysis.braking.TRAIL_STEER (0.08). Median 33 m on the owner's fastest F1 25 laps.

signals.name: Coasting distance
signals.summary: How far the car rolls with neither brake nor throttle between the end of braking and the throttle.
signals.notes: Both pedals below analysis.braking.BRAKE_OFF. Style detection reads it (10 m or more counts as coasting).

noise.metric: share of corners with 10 m or more, fastest laps
noise.note: The owner's fastest F1 25 laps of six sessions; the median corner has no coasting at all.

signals.name: Brake attack time
signals.summary: Time from first pressing the brake to reaching nine tenths of that stop's peak pressure.
signals.notes: BrakingEvent.time_to_peak_s (90% = technique.thresholds.PEAK_FRAC). Compared with the reference in the technique notes ("time_to_peak"), not coached; CornerDelta has no delta for it yet (time_to_peak_delta_s).

signals.name: Brake release time
signals.summary: Time from the last moment near the stop's peak brake pressure to the brake being fully off.
signals.notes: BrakingEvent.release_s (90% of peak to below BRAKE_OFF). Its shape (in one go, steadily, dropped then trailed, held then dropped late) is CornerInputs.release_shape, a word rather than a number.

signals.name: Brake at turn-in
signals.summary: How much brake was still on when the steering started to go in.
signals.notes: Turn-in = the reference lap's steering point (technique.line, TURN_IN_STEER_FRAC of the corner's peak steering).

signals.name: Braking while turning
signals.summary: Time with the brake on while the steering is past a quarter of the corner's peak, up to the slowest point.

signals.name: Throttle pick-up after the slowest point
signals.summary: How far after the corner's slowest point the throttle first came back.

signals.name: Throttle ramp time
signals.summary: Time from the throttle first coming back to full throttle.

signals.name: Throttle lifts on the exit
signals.summary: How many times the throttle dropped back by a clear amount between pick-up and full throttle.
signals.notes: A drop of technique.thresholds.LIFT_DROP (0.15) below the highest throttle so far. Counted up to the first full throttle only. Shown as a technique note and a habit ("lifted off the throttle on the exit more"), not coached.

signals.name: Lock-ups in the braking zone
signals.summary: How many times a wheel locked under braking at this corner.
signals.notes: CornerInputs.lockup.events: a wheel's slip ratio at or below technique.thresholds.LOCKUP_SLIP for LOCKUP_MIN_S with the brake on. Status abs_on when ABS is on (not counted). Wheel slip: F1 25 only.

signals.name: Wheelspin on the exit
signals.summary: How many times a rear wheel spun under throttle on the way out of this corner.
signals.notes: CornerInputs.wheelspin.events: a rear wheel's slip ratio at or above technique.thresholds.SPIN_SLIP for SPIN_MIN_S with the throttle on, from the slowest point to SPIN_AFTER_TRACK_OUT_M past the track-out. Wheel slip: F1 25 only.

signals.name: Entry balance
signals.summary: Front minus rear tyre slip angle at the limit on the way into the corner: clearly above zero is understeer.
signals.notes: The entry phase of technique.balance.lap_balance. Understeer at or above US_DIFF_DEG (3.0), oversteer at or below OS_DIFF_DEG.

signals.name: Mid-corner balance
signals.summary: Front minus rear tyre slip angle at the limit around the slowest point: clearly above zero is understeer.
signals.notes: The mid phase of technique.balance.lap_balance. Neutral real corners read about +0.4 to +2.9 degrees.

signals.name: Exit balance
signals.summary: Front minus rear tyre slip angle at the limit on the way out: clearly above zero is understeer.
signals.notes: The exit phase of technique.balance.lap_balance.

signals.name: Slide mid-corner
signals.summary: Whether the back of the car slid or needed a counter-steer around the corner's slowest point.
signals.notes: Body slip of SLIDE_BODY_SLIP_DEG towards oversteer for SLIDE_MIN_S, or a counter-steer run (technique.thresholds).

signals.name: Slide on the exit
signals.summary: Whether the back of the car slid or needed a counter-steer on the way out of the corner.
signals.notes: The exit phase of technique.balance.lap_balance.

signals.notes: Ed's BrakingEvent / CornerMetrics.pre_brake_coast_m: from a genuine lift (throttle was at PRE_BRAKE_ACCEL_PEDAL 0.5 or more) to the brake onset. The patch review found its scan running back over hundreds of metres.

signals.name: Throttle dip after pick-up
signals.summary: The largest drop in throttle after it first came back, as a share of full throttle.
signals.notes: Ed's CornerMetrics.throttle_dip_after_pickup_frac (his throttle_modulation rule: THROTTLE_DIP_FRAC 0.15).

signals.name: Throttle acceptance
signals.summary: Lateral g when full throttle arrives, as a share of the corner's peak lateral g.
signals.notes: Ed's CornerMetrics.throttle_acceptance. High = full throttle while still cornering hard; low = full throttle only once the car was nearly straight. Read from one sample in his patch. GT7 sends no lateral g.

signals.name: Throttle acceptance vs reference
signals.summary: Throttle acceptance on this lap minus the reference lap's; below zero means full throttle came with the car straighter.
signals.notes: Ed's CornerDelta.throttle_acceptance_delta (his rule: LOW_ACCEPTANCE_FRAC 0.15 below the reference).

signals.name: Steering corrections
signals.summary: How many times the steering changed direction within the corner.
signals.notes: Ed's CornerMetrics.steering_reversals (REVERSAL_MIN_RAD 0.03), compared with the reference (steering_reversals_delta). The rig check already counts reversals per lap on filtered steering with a gap method (rig.rig_check.count_reversals): reuse that per corner. AC's steering is not mapped; GT7's is approximate.

noise.metric: reversals per corner on clean laps, typical low
noise.note: Ed's counter on real F1 25 clean laps: 3 to 5 per corner, so a count alone is not a fault.

noise.metric: reversals per corner on clean laps, typical high

signals.name: Peak steering position vs reference
signals.summary: Where the steering peaked relative to the apex on this lap, minus the reference lap's; below zero is sooner.
signals.notes: Ed's CornerDelta.steering_peak_offset_delta_m from an argmax of |steering|, which jumps between peaks.

noise.note: Real F1 25 laps: the argmax moved to another steering peak of the segment, far from the apex.

signals.name: Turn-in time
signals.summary: Time from the start of turn-in to nine tenths of the corner's peak steering.
signals.notes: New: Ed's checklist asks for the steering rate at turn-in; a time to near-peak steering is the same idea in a unit the graph has. Nothing computes a steering rate yet (rig check: straight-line oscillation only).

signals.name: Unwind time
signals.summary: Time from the corner's peak steering back to a straight wheel on the way out.
signals.notes: New: Ed's checklist row on the mid-corner unwind rate. Not computed yet.

signals.name: Steering left at full throttle
signals.summary: How much of the corner's peak steering was still on when full throttle arrived.
signals.notes: New: Ed's checklist row on throttle before the steering unwinds. Pitwall places the pick-up only against the slowest point today (CornerInputs.pickup_vs_apex_m); nothing reads the steering at that moment.

signals.name: Grip used from apex to full throttle
signals.summary: The lowest combined g between the slowest point and full throttle, as a share of the corner's peak lateral g.
signals.notes: Ed's CornerMetrics.exit_grip_utilization_frac (LOW_GRIP_UTILIZATION_FRAC 0.5). GT7 sends no lateral g.

signals.name: Downshifts while braking
signals.summary: How many gear changes down were made during the braking zone.
signals.notes: Ed's BrakingEvent / CornerMetrics.downshifts (forward gears only).

signals.name: Downshifts without a blip
signals.summary: Downshifts with no throttle blip from the driver around the gear change.
signals.notes: Ed's BrakingEvent / CornerMetrics.missed_blips: no throttle at BLIP_PEDAL (0.15) within BLIP_WINDOW_S (0.25 s) of the change. With paddles and auto-blip the game blips for the driver, so the pedal never shows it.

signals.name: Gear change while turning
signals.summary: Whether a gear change was made while the steering was past half of the corner's peak.
signals.notes: Ed's CornerMetrics.gear_change_while_turning (GEAR_CHANGE_STEER_FRAC 0.5).

signals.name: Aero crossover speed
signals.summary: The speed above which the car's sustainable lateral g starts to rise with speed, as aerodynamic load builds.
signals.notes: Ed's technique/aero_crossover.py (AeroCrossover.crossover_kph): a flat floor of lateral g below the crossover and a rise with the square of the speed above it, fitted on 10 km/h bins of a high percentile. Not wired.

signals.name: Line at track-out vs reference
signals.summary: How far the car was from the reference lap's line at the reference's track-out point.
signals.notes: The "track_out" entry of LapCornerTechnique.line (technique/session.py, POINT_KEYS: turn_in, apex, track_out), from technique/line.py's lateral offsets against the reference lap's line: above zero is tighter (towards the inside of the corner) when the inside is known, else the distance without a side; laps wider or tighter beyond LINE_NOTABLE_M are counted. After the session only; needs the adapter's ground plane (position).

faults.name: Braking early
faults.summary: Braking started clearly earlier than on the reference lap, and the corner cost time.
faults.notes: Rule: braking point at least BRAKE_POINT_M before the reference's and at least MIN_TIME_LOSS_S lost. Today's texts: "you're braking about N m earlier than your reference (lap R), losing X s", simple "you braked about N m earlier than on your reference lap", short "braked N m earlier", radio "braking N m earlier than your reference". It is in LATER_BRAKING_FIXES: its "sorted" (which praises the later braking) is said only when the corner also got faster.

measured.note: 74 of 667 corner-laps of six real F1 25 sessions, each lap against the fastest earlier clean lap.

faults.name: Overdriving the entry
faults.summary: Braking started clearly later than on the reference lap, but the car came out of the corner slower and the corner cost time.
faults.notes: Rule: braking point at least BRAKE_POINT_M after the reference's, exit at least EXIT_SPEED_KPH slower and at least MIN_TIME_LOSS_S lost (only when brake_early did not fire). Today's texts: "you're braking N m later than your reference but exiting N km/h slower - the later braking isn't paying off", simple "the later braking did not pay off - you came out N km/h slower", short "braked later, N km/h slower out", radio "braking N m later but exiting N km/h slower". The rule's own texts are older than the graph's constraints; the graph's advice says the same without the phrasings the constraints catch.

measured.note: 59 of 667 corner-laps of six real F1 25 sessions.

faults.name: Too fast at the apex
faults.summary: The slowest point of the corner was clearly faster than on the reference lap, but the exit was slower and the corner cost time.
faults.notes: Rule: minimum speed at least MIN_SPEED_KPH above the reference's, exit at least EXIT_SPEED_KPH slower and at least MIN_TIME_LOSS_S lost (only when low_min_speed did not fire). Today's texts: "you're carrying N km/h more into the apex but exiting N km/h slower - too much entry speed is compromising the exit", simple "the extra speed into the corner cost you on the way out: N km/h slower", short "faster in, N km/h slower out", radio "N km/h too much into the apex, exit N km/h down".

measured.note: 14 of 667 corner-laps of six real F1 25 sessions.

faults.name: Low minimum speed
faults.summary: The slowest point of the corner was clearly slower than on the reference lap, and the corner cost time.
faults.notes: Rule (observations_for_comparison): minimum speed at least MIN_SPEED_KPH below the reference and at least MIN_TIME_LOSS_S lost through the corner. Today's texts: "minimum speed is N km/h lower than your reference", simple "you were N km/h slower at the slowest point of the corner", short "N km/h slower mid-corner".

measured.note: 278 of 667 corner-laps of six real F1 25 sessions: the most common point by far. Of those, over_braking was named on 32 (12%) and early_turn_in on 16 (6%).

faults.name: Late to full throttle
faults.summary: Full throttle came clearly later on the way out than on the reference lap, and the corner cost time.
faults.notes: Rule: full throttle at least THROTTLE_M later than the reference's and at least MIN_TIME_LOSS_S lost. Today's texts: "you're reaching full throttle N m later than your reference", simple "you got back to full throttle about N m later than on your reference lap", short "full throttle N m later", radio "full throttle N m later than your reference". Ed's checklist: the rule alone cannot tell an exit short of grip from grip left unused; the causes traction_limited and ready_earlier do, on F1 25 (tyre slip). On GT7 variants A and B the throttle is after traction control.

measured.note: 124 of 667 corner-laps of six real F1 25 sessions.

faults.name: Coasting
faults.summary: Clearly more distance off both pedals between the brake and the throttle than on the reference lap, and the corner cost time.
faults.notes: Rule: at least COAST_M more coasting than the reference and at least MIN_TIME_LOSS_S lost. Today's texts: "about N m more coasting (no brake, no throttle) than your reference between brake release and throttle", simple "you spent about N m more off both pedals than on your reference lap", short "N m more coasting", radio "N m more coasting than your reference". Style-aware without changing who gets it: the rule compares with the driver's own reference, so a driver who coasts to the apex on purpose (coast_to_apex, Ed's brief point 8) is told only when this lap coasted clearly more than their own faster lap. The advice differs by detected braking style (trail / straight_line); the owner's fastest F1 25 laps coast at only 15% of corners (pitwall_style_review).

measured.note: 24 of 667 corner-laps of six real F1 25 sessions (a driver who rarely coasts). Of those, early_brake_release was named on 11 and waiting_for_rotation on 9.

faults.name: Good exit
faults.summary: The car came out of the corner clearly faster than on the reference lap, and the corner gained time.
faults.notes: Praise. Rule: exit at least EXIT_SPEED_KPH faster than the reference and at least MIN_TIME_LOSS_S gained. Today's texts: "good - exit speed is up N km/h on your reference and you gained X s there", simple "good exit - you came out N km/h faster than on your reference lap", short "good exit, N km/h faster", radio "good exit, N km/h up".

measured.note: 147 of 667 corner-laps of six real F1 25 sessions.

faults.name: Incident
faults.summary: The corner lost far more time than a technique difference could (a spin, contact, a trip off the track or a slow-down), so it gives no technique advice.
faults.notes: Rule (is_incident): at least INCIDENT_LOSS_S lost at the corner, or a slowest point below INCIDENT_SPEED_FRAC of a reference of at least INCIDENT_MIN_REF_KPH. Reported once, kept out of averages, habits and technique advice, and never said on the radio (the driver knows). Filed under mid-corner because it reads the whole corner and its slowest point. Today's texts: "lost N s - that looks like an incident (spin, contact, off-track or a slow-down), so no technique advice from this corner on this lap", short "incident, no advice this lap".

measured.note: 14 of 681 corner-laps of six real F1 25 sessions.

faults.name: Slow brake attack
faults.summary: The brake took longer to reach its peak pressure than on the reference lap: a squeeze up to the pedal rather than a quick, firm press.
faults.notes: Ed's brief point 2 and checklist row "slow ramp-up". Ed marked it not covered; the review found the attack time (time_to_peak_s) already measured and compared with the reference in the technique notes after the session. Ed's root-cause patch would coach it at 0.05 s slower than the reference and losing (SLOW_BRAKE_ATTACK_S, not validated): that sits well inside the lap-to-reference spread (time_to_peak_delta_s), so it is not coached. With the game's braking assist on, brake notes are muted.

measured.note: 667 corner-laps of real F1 25 laps, attack 0.05 s slower than the reference and the corner losing time.

measured.metric: corner-laps 0.05 s or more off the reference
measured.note: Either way: the attack time varies that much from lap to lap on its own.

faults.name: Abrupt brake release
faults.summary: The brake pressure came off in one quick drop, quicker than on the reference lap, instead of easing away as the car slowed.
faults.notes: Ed's brief point 3 and checklist row "abrupt / stepped release" (he marked it built: the technique notes describe the release time and shape - in one go, steadily, dropped then trailed, held then dropped late - after the session). His root-cause patch would coach a release 0.05 s quicker than the reference and losing (ABRUPT_BRAKE_RELEASE_S, not validated): inside the spread (release_time_delta_s), so it is not coached.

measured.note: 667 corner-laps of real F1 25 laps, release 0.05 s quicker than the reference and the corner losing time.

measured.metric: corner-laps 0.05 s or more off the reference

faults.name: Throttle sawtooth
faults.summary: The throttle went on and off repeatedly on the way out instead of rising to full in one go.
faults.notes: Ed's checklist row "sawtooth (repeated on / off)" and brief point 10. Ed marked it not covered; the review found throttle_lifts counting it after the session (a technique note and a habit), up to the first full throttle only. On GT7 variants A and B the throttle is after traction control, so the car's own cuts would count: no game gating yet.

faults.name: Lap-to-lap scatter
faults.summary: The braking point or the slowest speed at a corner moved around a lot from one lap to the next.
faults.notes: Ed's checklist row and one of his suggested next steps. The review: the spread per corner exists after the session (report, AI engineer facts, corner cards), not live; the live consistency_ratio is the share of laps past a rule's threshold, not a spread. No threshold yet.

faults.name: Lock-up
faults.summary: A wheel stopped turning under braking, so the tyre slid instead of gripping and the car slowed less well.
faults.notes: Ed's checklist row "lockups / wheelspin" (built). Counted per corner (technique.inputs) and per lap by car health (carhealth/slip.py), which says lock-ups on the radio; not a coaching kind. With ABS on there is no lock-up to count (abs_on), hence abs_off. Tyre slip: F1 25 only. Linked to the progressive release: as the car slows it has less downforce, so the same pressure late in the stop locks a wheel (Ed's brief point 3).

faults.name: Wheelspin on the exit
faults.summary: A rear wheel spun under throttle on the way out of the corner, so the car accelerated less than the throttle asked.
faults.notes: Ed's checklist row "lockups / wheelspin" (built). Per corner (technique.inputs) and per lap (carhealth/slip.py, said on the radio only with traction control off or medium: with it full, about one a lap is normal). Tyre slip: F1 25 only. Evidence for the cause traction_limited.

faults.name: Understeer or oversteer at a corner
faults.summary: The front tyres (understeer) or the rear tyres (oversteer) reached their limit first at this corner, lap after lap.
faults.notes: Ed's checklist row "driver vs car under / oversteer" (built: technique/balance.py, F1 25 only). A symptom must recur (2 or more laps, half the laps with data); one the session's best lap also had is the car's (setup suggestions), one it did not have points at how the corner was driven (entry speed or line). Shown on the Technique page, not coached.

faults.name: Track left unused on the exit
faults.summary: The car ran out of the corner tighter than on the reference lap, leaving part of the track's width unused on the way out.
faults.notes: Ed's brief point 12. The racing line analysis compares each lap's line with the reference at turn-in, apex and track-out (wider / tighter beyond LINE_NOTABLE_M) after the session; it is shown, not coached. Relative to the driver's own reference lap, never to the track's edges, which no game sends. Needs a position channel (read on F1 25 and a GT7 capture).

faults.name: Brake pressed twice
faults.summary: In one stop the brake pressure dipped and then rose again to a second peak, instead of one clean release.
faults.notes: Ed's checklist row "double hump (lift, re-apply)". He marked it not covered because braking.py merges stabs closer than MERGE_GAP_S into one event; the review rated that half right: the rig check counts re-applications per lap (not per corner, no peak or duration floor), and a decoded Austria lap shows one event peaking at 0.95, dipping to 0.42 and back to 0.89. Ed's detector: his HUMP_DIP_FRAC and HUMP_MIN_FRAC (not validated).

measured.note: 667 to 681 corner-laps of real F1 25 laps.

faults.name: Brake and throttle overlap
faults.summary: The brake and the throttle were pressed at the same time when only one of them was meant to be.
faults.notes: Ed's checklist row "unintentional brake / throttle overlap" (he marked it partly covered: lock-up gating only). Not a fault for a left-foot braker, whose overlap is the technique (left_foot_braking): the driver's Context has no left-foot braking trait yet, so the fault cannot say so with a condition; it must not coach until it can. On F1 25 it fired on two thirds of corner-laps because the game reports a steady 0.10 throttle under braking (Ed's floor is 0.10): a game artefact, not the driver.

measured.note: 455 of 681 corner-laps of real F1 25 laps; F1 25 reports throttle 0.10 under braking (3 to 110 samples a lap).

faults.name: Lift before braking
faults.summary: The throttle came off well before the braking point and the car rolled with no pedal pressed before braking began.
faults.notes: Ed's brief point 1 and checklist row "lift-and-coast before the brake zone" (his patch adds it as pre_brake_coast_m). Not a fault when the race strategy asks for lift and coast to save fuel (fuel_save_lift_and_coast, Context fuel_saving; the strategy already knows it: strategy/engine.py lift_coast): it needs a "not fuel saving" condition before it can coach. The review found the scan reporting hundreds of metres (it runs back past the lift).

measured.note: 667 to 681 corner-laps of real F1 25 laps; inflated by the scan bug.

faults.name: Sawing at the wheel
faults.summary: More steering corrections back and forth through the corner than on the reference lap, as if fighting the car's balance.
faults.notes: Ed's brief point 7 and checklist row "sawing mid-corner (multiple sign changes)". His counter finds 3 to 5 reversals per corner on clean laps; the rig check's filtered, gap-based counter (per lap) is the better base. AC's steering is not mapped; GT7's is approximate.

measured.note: 667 to 681 corner-laps of real F1 25 laps: one more reversal than the reference is within the noise.

faults.name: Snatched turn-in
faults.summary: The steering went in with a sudden jerk instead of one smooth movement to the corner's angle.
faults.notes: Ed's brief point 7 and checklist row "snatched / aggressive turn-in (steering rate)". Nothing measures a steering rate per corner yet (the review); compared with the driver's own reference because a hairpin and a kink need very different rates.

faults.name: Early apex
faults.summary: The car reached the tightest part of the corner sooner than on the reference lap, which tends to push it wide on the exit or force a second correction.
faults.notes: Ed's checklist row "early apex (steering peak before the geometric apex, second correction)"; he marked it partly covered (the line thresholds measure offset, not apex timing). His detector takes the argmax of the steering, which jumps between peaks (values like -289 m). The slowest point's position (min_speed_pos_delta_m) is computed but noisy; the cause early_turn_in uses it with a wide margin.

measured.note: 667 to 681 corner-laps of real F1 25 laps; many from argmax jumps.

faults.name: Stepped throttle after a slow apex
faults.summary: After a slow middle of the corner the throttle went on, off and on again instead of one smooth application.
faults.notes: Ed's brief point 10 and self-check (an on-off-on throttle means the car arrived too slow), his checklist row "released too early for the apex" and his throttle_modulation detector (a dip of THROTTLE_DIP_FRAC after pick-up with a slow apex; the root-cause patch splits it into over-braking and early turn-in). The self-check stays a review-only explanation in the causes' advice, tied to the driver's own faster laps; the fix Ed suggested with it is an instruction the constraints reject, so it is not in the graph.

measured.note: 667 to 681 corner-laps of real F1 25 laps.

faults.name: Low throttle acceptance
faults.summary: Full throttle arrived with the car cornering much less hard than on the reference lap, as if the throttle waited for the car to straighten.
faults.notes: Ed's checklist KPI "throttle acceptance" (lateral g at the first full throttle over the corner's peak lateral g). His patch's wording is inverted: it says the throttle went in before the car was ready, but a lower acceptance means full throttle came with the car straighter. Read from one sample. GT7 sends no lateral g.

measured.note: 667 to 681 corner-laps of real F1 25 laps.

faults.name: Throttle before the steering unwinds
faults.summary: Full throttle came with most of the steering still on, which pushes the car wide on the way out (power understeer).
faults.notes: Ed's brief point 11 and checklist rows "early throttle before steering unwinds (power understeer)" and "mid-corner unwind rate". Nothing reads the steering at pick-up or full throttle yet (the review); the confirming signal exists on F1 25: exit understeer (technique/balance.py).

faults.name: Unused grip on the exit
faults.summary: Between the apex and full throttle the tyres worked well below their limit: the cornering load fell away before the acceleration built up.
faults.notes: Ed's checklist row "unused grip: G-G points near the centre, transitions not overlapped" and his suggested G-G diagram (Pitwall has none; Compare gains his g-force charts). Combined g needs lateral and longitudinal g: GT7 sends no lateral g. His patch skips it when late_throttle already fired at the corner.

measured.note: 667 to 681 corner-laps of real F1 25 laps.

faults.name: Missed rev-match blip
faults.summary: A downshift under braking with no throttle blip to match the engine speed, which can unsettle the rear of the car.
faults.notes: Ed's brief point 4 and his root-cause patch (downshifts and missed blips, computed, not a rule). With paddles and auto-blip the game blips for the driver and the pedal never shows it, so it applies to an H-pattern gearbox only (unknown gearbox = does not apply). Ed's synthetic generator never blips, so on synthetic laps it reads every downshift as missed.

measured.metric: real downshifts with no driver blip
measured.note: Real F1 25 laps with paddle shifts: the game blips, so this measures the game, not the driver.

faults.name: Gear change while cornering
faults.summary: A gear change made with the steering well wound on, which can upset the car's balance in the middle of the corner.
faults.notes: Ed's checklist row; his patch computes it but leaves it out of coaching because on his generated F1 data it fired on nearly every corner (paddle-shift drivers routinely change gear while still turning). Pitwall's judgement [H]: with paddles a mid-corner shift is routine, with an H-pattern gearbox it takes a hand off the wheel and a clutch while the car is loaded, so it applies to an H-pattern gearbox only. Upshifts on the exit are normal (Ed's brief point 12).

faults.name: Entry understeer from the brake release
faults.summary: The car pushed wide on the way in after the brake pressure came off sharply, taking load off the front tyres just as they began to turn.
faults.notes: Ed's checklist row "entry understeer from release shape" (he marked it partly covered). The balance's with_braking flag only qualifies setup suggestions; the release shape is never compared between understeer and neutral laps yet. F1 25 only (tyre slip).

faults.name: Aero crossover
faults.summary: Below a certain speed the car's grip comes from its tyres and suspension alone; above it, downforce adds grip that grows with speed. A property of the car, not a fault of the driver.
faults.notes: Ed's checklist: the most lateral g a car can hold is flat at low speed (mechanical grip) and rises with the square of the speed once aero adds load; the crossover is lower for an F1 car than a GT3 car. His technique/aero_crossover.py fits it (not wired). Background for which corners are grip-limited by the tyres and which by downforce; context_only rather than planned because it describes the car, not how it was driven.

causes.name: Over-braking
causes.summary: More braking than on the reference lap on the way in, so the car reached the corner slower than on that lap.
causes.notes: Ed's brief: a lift after the throttle has started means the car arrived too slow, from too much braking or an early turn-in; his self-check reads an on-off-on throttle the same way. Thresholds are the coaching rules' own floors. Named on 32 of 278 low_min_speed points (12%).

discriminators.test: braked at least 8 m earlier than on the reference lap
discriminators.note: 8 m is analysis.coaching.BRAKE_POINT_M, the brake_early rule's floor.

discriminators.test: at least 4 km/h slower at the corner entry than on the reference lap
discriminators.note: 4 km/h is analysis.coaching.MIN_SPEED_KPH, the low_min_speed rule's floor.

causes.name: Early turn-in
causes.summary: The car was turned towards the apex sooner than on the reference lap, so the tightest part of the corner came sooner and the car had to slow more for it.
causes.notes: Ed's brief point 10 (a lift once on the throttle comes from over-braking or turning in too early) and his root-cause patch, which tells the two apart with peak steering 10 m sooner than usual (EARLY_APEX_M; its argmax jumps). Pitwall uses the slowest point's position instead, which is computed but noisy (clean-lap quartiles -14 and +17 m), so the margin is wide and the entry must not have been slower (that is over_braking). Named on 16 of 278 low_min_speed points (6%); a 10 m margin would name it on 71 (26%), mostly noise.

discriminators.test: the slowest point came at least 20 m sooner than on the reference lap
discriminators.note: [H] Outside the clean-lap quartiles of this delta (-14 and +17 m on real F1 25 laps).

discriminators.test: reached the corner entry no more than 4 km/h slower than on the reference lap
discriminators.note: Keeps it apart from over_braking, which needs a slower entry (analysis.coaching.MIN_SPEED_KPH).

causes.name: Less grip
causes.summary: The tyres were sliding at this corner on this lap (a slide, understeer or a locked wheel), so the car could not hold the speed of the reference lap.
causes.notes: Past the edge of the tyres' grip in any direction the car slides: a locked wheel under braking, the front pushing wide (understeer) or the rear stepping out (oversteer). Evidence from tyre slip, so F1 25 only; on other games these are unmeasured and the cause is never named. Wheelspin is left out: it comes after the slowest point, so it is evidence for traction_limited (late_throttle) instead. These are this lap's values, not a difference from the reference lap.

discriminators.test: the back of the car slid or needed a counter-steer around the slowest point
the front tyres were sliding clearly more than the rears around the slowest point (understeer)
a wheel locked in the braking zone

causes.name: Traction-limited exit
causes.summary: The rear tyres spun or the car slid on the way out, so full throttle could not come as soon as on the reference lap.
causes.notes: Ed's checklist: late_throttle alone cannot tell an exit short of grip from grip left unused. Too much throttle for the grip spins the driven wheels and can start oversteer; the driver then waits or lifts. Tyre slip and body slip: F1 25 only. With traction control full some wheelspin is normal (car health keeps those off the radio).

discriminators.test: a rear wheel spun under throttle on the way out
the back of the car slid or needed a counter-steer on the way out

causes.name: Car ready before the throttle
causes.summary: On the way out the car showed no wheelspin, slide or understeer, yet full throttle came later than on the reference lap: the grip was there before the throttle.
causes.notes: Ed's checklist row "over-cautious exit (full throttle late with no grip loss)". The spec also names the steering already unwound and less combined g than the reference: those signals are not computed yet (steering_at_full_throttle_frac, exit_grip_utilization_frac, throttle_acceptance_delta); add them here as discriminators when they are. F1 25 only (tyre slip); an exit balance that was not measured (no at-the-limit samples) names nothing.

discriminators.test: no wheelspin on the way out
no slide or counter-steer on the way out
no clear understeer on the way out

causes.name: Early brake release
causes.summary: Braking ended sooner than on the reference lap, which opened a longer gap with neither pedal pressed before the throttle.
causes.notes: A longer coast opens at one end or the other: here the brake end moved (waiting_for_rotation: the throttle end). Published telemetry guides read a flat gap between the brake and the throttle as time lost; Pitwall only describes it. Named on 11 of 24 coasting points.

discriminators.test: braking ended at least 8 m sooner than on the reference lap
discriminators.note: [H] 8 m is analysis.coaching.BRAKE_POINT_M, the floor for a braking point difference.

causes.name: Waiting for the car to rotate

sources.name: Professional Motorsport Data Analysis: braking performance - braking technique
sources.summary: A data-analysis lesson on reading the brake trace. The gap between lifting off the throttle and braking should be short. Pressure builds quickly, and the peak belongs at the start of the stop; then it bleeds off smoothly: steadily in a downforce car as the aero grip falls with speed, while a low-downforce car tends to hold nearer its peak for part of the stop. When trail braking, the pressure falls roughly in step with the steering going in. Peaking, backing off and pressing again near turn-in is a common error. Smooth inputs throughout; left-foot braking is optional, and many amateur drivers keep a better feel braking with the right foot. Read 2026-10-15.

sources.name: The art of releasing the brakes
sources.summary: Argues that how the brake comes off matters more for corner speed than how hard the stop is: a hard first application, then a release that begins before the car has lost too much speed and keeps load on the front tyres as the car turns in, which helps it rotate. With the pedal fully off the car is still slowing, and the steering itself scrubs speed. How long the brake stays on depends on the corner: deeper into hairpins, a quicker hand-over to the throttle in medium corners. Read 2026-10-15.

sources.name: Trail braking
sources.summary: Trail braking keeps the brake on past the start of the turn and eases it off, fully released somewhere between turn-in and the apex, so weight stays on the front tyres and the car turns in and rotates; it is used most in slow corners and takes finesse, and too much of it can make the front tyres slide or lock the rears. The conventional alternative finishes all braking before the steering goes in, and beginner training (motorcycles) teaches all the slowing before the turn. Read 2026-10-15.

sources.name: Heel-and-toe shifting
sources.summary: With a manual gearbox and a clutch, a downshift while braking needs the engine speeded up to match the wheels in the lower gear: the right foot brakes and blips the throttle at the same time. Without the blip the engine drags on the wheels for a moment, a jolt that can unsettle the car in a turn. Some cars blip for the driver on downshifts. Read 2026-10-15.

sources.name: Left-foot braking
sources.summary: Braking with the left foot while the right stays on the throttle: less time moving between pedals, revs (and turbo boost) kept up, and a way to adjust load transfer and help the car rotate. Cars with no clutch pedal - paddle shifts, automatic gears, karts, many single-seaters - make it possible; brake and throttle overlap on purpose in this technique. Read 2026-10-15.

sources.name: Racing line
sources.summary: The racing line uses the full width of the track - in from the outside edge, the inside at the apex, back out to the outside on exit - to open the corner's radius; a later apex suits slower corners and gives a faster exit, while an early apex gives a quicker entry but a slower exit and is a common beginner error. Read 2026-10-15.

sources.name: Does an earlier throttle application mean a better corner exit?
sources.summary: Argues that an early throttle pick-up often costs time: it makes the car push and keeps steering on at the exit. Picking up once the car has rotated, then one smooth, steady application all the way to full with no easing off, and opening the steering as it goes on, reaches full throttle sooner. Read 2026-10-15.

sources.name: 'Lift and coast': why F1 drivers are told to save fuel
sources.summary: Lift and coast: when the race needs fuel saved, the driver lifts off the throttle a little before the braking zone, rolls, then brakes at the usual point. Fuel burns fastest at full throttle at top speed and the car's drag slows it anyway, so it saves the most fuel for the least time, and it eases engine and brake temperatures too. Read 2026-10-15.

sources.name: Sim racing telemetry for beginners: turn data into faster laps
sources.summary: A beginner's guide to the traces: a firm brake application then a smooth release; a slow build loses deceleration, and a sudden drop can leave the car pushing at the apex; a throttle that saws up and down points to an overdriven exit fighting wheelspin; steering zig-zags inside one corner point to a balance struggle; a long gap off both pedals usually means the braking finished too soon. Advises a baseline of clean laps, a reference-lap overlay and one change at a time. Cited by Ed for his checklist; read 2026-10-15.

sources.name: Analyzing driver data
sources.summary: Driver data analysis: plot laps against distance and find the loss against a reference lap; compare brake points, pressure and how deep the trail braking goes; get to full throttle on exit and watch for brake and throttle overlap; jerky or stair-stepped steering, especially under braking, unsettles the car; on a g-g plot, braking g falling away before cornering g builds shows braking and turning not blended; scatter across laps shows inconsistency. Cited by Ed for his checklist; read 2026-10-15.

sources.name: Fundamentals: the traction circle (iRacing career guide, second season)
sources.summary: A tyre has one budget of grip shared between braking, cornering and acceleration. Novices are taught to brake, steer and accelerate one at a time, which is safe but leaves grip unused; braking at the limit and then steering asks too much, so the front tyres lock or push wide, and the brake eases off as the steering goes in. At the apex the car is on its full cornering grip with little or no pedal, then the throttle builds as the steering unwinds. Cited by Ed for his checklist; read 2026-10-15.

sources.name: Understeer and oversteer
sources.summary: Understeer: the car turns less than the steering asks and runs wide at the limit; oversteer: it turns more and tends to spin. Braking that puts too much load on the front tyres can make them slide, and enough power at the rear wheels can start oversteer. Cited by Ed for his checklist; read 2026-10-15.
